question: Which of FTG, Calian, and Magellan is a high-quality, reasonably priced beneficiary of Canadian defence/Build Canada spending and AI?

currency_policy.note: All three TSX quotes and issuer financial statements are CAD; no USD/CAD conversion was applied.

investor_context.residency: California resident, Canadian citizen, US MFJ
investor_context.note: Research output is evidence and valuation discipline, not a trade instruction or reserve-deployment assumption.

ranking.label: best relative candidate, wait for margin of safety
ranking.rationale: Only name with demonstrated AI delivery, a diversified mission-critical moat, roughly C$1 billion of defence backlog, and a materially lower EBITDA multiple than peers. Conventional cash conversion is far weaker than management's preferred operating-free-cash-flow metric, so C$83.25 is reasonable rather than cheap.

ranking.label: highest apparent operating quality, valuation too demanding
ranking.rationale: Excellent backlog, book-to-bill and current margins with a high-reliability electronics moat, but temporary pricing and classified-program ramps contribute to peak-looking results. At about 20x TTM adjusted EBITDA and under a 3% approximate FCF yield, it is not a cheap defence or AI beneficiary.

ranking.label: strong earnings momentum, weakest cash/governance fit
ranking.rationale: Q2 earnings accelerated and Canadian sovereign-production opportunities are real, but most revenue remains commercial/global, MOUs are conditional, TTM after-capex cash flow is negative, and a 75.4% controlling shareholder materially weakens minority governance.

comparative_conclusion.portfolio_fit: For a 2-3 year house horizon and single-income recession sensitivity, none qualifies as an immediate high-conviction cheap purchase at the supplied closes. CGY merits the first watch; FTG requires a larger valuation reset; MAL requires both a lower price and evidence that earnings convert to cash.
comparative_conclusion.ai_conclusion: CGY has actual deployed AI/ML projects but discloses no AI-specific revenue, margin, contract value or backlog. FTG and MAL disclose no attributable AI revenue. AI should not support a valuation premium for any of the three on current evidence.

ttm.method: Revenue and net income are issuer-period arithmetic. Adjusted EBITDA is issuer-disclosed. FCF combines annual operating-cash-less-leases with interim issuer FCF and is only approximately comparable.

growth_quality.organic_vs_acquired: Q3 Circuits growth came from operational improvement, short-term pricing premiums and FX; Aerospace included C$2.2M organic growth, a C$0.5M cancellation charge and FX. FLYHT acquisition affected the prior-year base and share count.
growth_quality.warning: Temporary pricing premiums and undisclosed classified-program ramp make the Q3 margin unsuitable as a normalized base without a haircut.

backlog.quality: Purchase-order backlog with strong near-term coverage, but subject to FX/cancellation and opaque classified programs.

cash_conversion.assessment: Strong current conversion, but the issuer FCF definition includes FX and annual/interim labels are not fully identical.

customer_and_program_risk.programs: Classified defence programs and global aerospace customers; geography/value of classified ramps not disclosed.
customer_and_program_risk.canada_budget_link: plausible but unquantified; customer-location data show only 7.1% of nine-month revenue in Canada and do not reveal the ultimate government/program funding source

moat_and_roic.moat: Customer-qualified high-reliability complex PCBs and cockpit electronics, certifications, engineering customization, long program lives.
moat_and_roic.roic_caveat: Analytical estimate using adjusted EBITDA less approximate D&A, assumed 25% tax, and point-in-time invested capital; boosted by current pricing/mix.

ai.evidence: No AI disclosure found in Q3 report or FY2025 AIF.

valuation.entry_logic: 14-16x TTM adjusted EBITDA and 25-30x TTM EPS imply approximately C$22-26; prefer low end because disclosed temporary pricing helps current margins.

bear_case: Short-term pricing premiums and classified-program ramps normalize faster than expected.
Customer concentration and opaque purchase-order backlog increase downside if one platform slips.
USD/CAD, tariffs and multinational manufacturing exposure complicate a pure Build Canada thesis.
Current multiple and low FCF yield leave little recession margin of safety.
decision_changing_gaps: Normalized margin excluding pricing premiums and cancellation/classified-program effects.
Classified-program geography, value, duration and Canadian government linkage.
A consistently defined TTM free-cash-flow reconciliation.
Organic growth excluding all acquisition and FX effects by segment.

ttm.method: Issuer-period arithmetic; conventional FCF equals IFRS operating cash less capex. Issuer OFCF removes working-capital changes and acquisition costs and does not deduct capex.

growth_quality.organic_vs_acquired: Quarter organic growth 16% and acquisitive growth 4%; nine-month organic growth 11% and acquisitive growth 6%.

backlog.quality: Large and diversified through FY2030, but realizable backlog exceeds contractual performance obligations and fee-for-service effort can change. The issuer says approximately C$1B is defence backlog; it does not disclose that this amount is Canadian defence backlog.

segment_and_geography.warning: Defence & Space is broader than defence, and company revenue is not a pure Canadian-budget exposure.

cash_conversion.assessment: Weak on conventional cash measures and materially flattered by issuer OFCF adjustments.

governance.assessment: strongest minority governance of the three

moat_and_roic.moat: Long trusted relationships with Canadian and allied defence customers plus specialized space, cyber, training, nuclear and healthcare credentials.
moat_and_roic.roic_caveat: Analytical estimate based on adjusted EBITDA less D&A, assumed 25% tax, and point-in-time debt/equity/cash; acquisition accounting matters.

delivered_projects: nuclear shift-log LLM/multi-agent proof of concept
ai.assessment: real delivery evidence, no basis to isolate AI revenue or premium

valuation.entry_logic: 8-9x TTM adjusted EBITDA implies C$61.6-70.3; 15-17x adjusted EPS implies C$66.8-75.7. Overlap supports C$65-72 while demanding compensation for weak cash conversion.
valuation.assessment: best relative valuation, not clearly cheap on cash flow

bear_case: Reported adjusted profit continues to convert poorly into cash as working capital and capex consume funds.
Backlog realizability estimates and fee-for-service effort prove optimistic.
Acquisition goodwill/intangibles lead to impairment or further capital needs.
The Defence & Space label overstates pure defence exposure and AI never becomes financially material.
decision_changing_gaps: AI-specific revenue, backlog, margin and repeat-customer disclosures.
Contractual defence backlog split by Canada, allies, fixed-price versus fee-for-service, and funded versus option years.
Evidence that conventional FCF conversion can approach adjusted EBITDA conversion claims without working-capital add-backs.
Organic margins and returns by segment after acquisition integration.

ttm.method: Issuer-period arithmetic using FY2025 less H1 2025 plus H1 2026.

growth_quality.organic_vs_acquired: No acquisition contribution identified. Growth was program volume, pricing/mix and FX; European growth explicitly included favourable FX.

backlog.quality: Firm program obligations with long aerospace lives; Q2 filing does not update this figure. Industry aircraft backlog is not Magellan backlog.

cash_conversion.assessment: Weakest of the three: first-half working capital used C$55.9M and TTM capex exceeded operating cash.

customer_and_program_risk.programs: Global commercial aircraft, engine and defence programs; M72 sovereign production, TKMS teaming, and conditional Gripen/F414 MOU create Canadian optionality.
customer_and_program_risk.canada_budget_link: plausible but recent announcements largely lack value or are conditional

moat_and_roic.moat: Qualified/sole-source positions, difficult aerospace manufacturing and MRO capability, long program lives and contracts extending into the 2030s.
moat_and_roic.roic_caveat: Analytical estimate based on adjusted EBITDA less D&A, assumed 25% tax and point-in-time invested capital; heavy reinvestment makes accounting return exceed current cash return.

ai.evidence: No AI product, contract or revenue disclosure found in Q2 or FY2025 reports.

valuation.entry_logic: 9-11x TTM adjusted EBITDA implies C$22.9-28.1; 22-26x TTM EPS implies C$22.9-27.0. Governance and negative FCF argue for the lower portion.
valuation.assessment: earnings momentum is priced while cash and governance risks remain

bear_case: Commercial aerospace cycle or supply constraints reverse recent volume/margin improvement.
Receivables, contract assets, inventory and capex keep consuming cash despite accounting earnings.
Canadian defence MOUs/teamings do not become funded awards, or Gripen is not selected.
The 75.4% controller and related-party structure limit minority influence and market liquidity.
decision_changing_gaps: Updated company-specific firm performance obligations after FY2025.
M72 contract value and delivery schedule; funded value of submarine work; probability-weighted F414 outcome.
Working-capital normalization timeline and maintenance versus growth capex split.
Customer/platform concentration by named program and contract margin.

cross_company_material_contradictions_or.issue: The issuer's OFCF adds back working-capital changes and acquisition costs and excludes capex, producing C$72.2M TTM versus about C$26.3M conventional pre-lease FCF.
cross_company_material_contradictions_or.status: definition difference, not an arithmetic contradiction

cross_company_material_contradictions_or.issue: The third-party forward EPS field is implausibly below the primary-document TTM earnings arithmetic; primary reported net income was used instead.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA and earnings surged while operating cash and after-capex cash deteriorated materially.
cross_company_material_contradictions_or.status: economic divergence requiring cash conversion evidence
